continuity_scope: Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord, Digital Eclipse's full-3D remake official-release version of 23 May 2024, English Drecom IP-holder release witness. It is a remake built directly on the 1981 Apple II code but is treated as a separate 2024 release/presentation. Original Apple II text, early-access state, ports, sequels, other Wizardry IP works, later patches, and localization variants are excluded from detailed character claims.
work_or_witnesses: Drecom: Official release version of Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord available on consoles & PC
Drecom: With Wizardry 43rd anniversary official IP notice
coverage_rule: All stable named dramatic individuals directly identified and functionally described in the selected official 2024 remake story witness: Trebor, the mad overlord who orders the party into the labyrinth, and Werdna, the evil wizard who stole the amulet. Player-created adventurers are explicitly excluded. No other NPC, monster, party member, or named individual is added without an equivalent individual claim-level official profile or direct-game locator.
omissions: All player-created adventurers and parties, including names, classes, races, alignments, builds, deaths, spell choices, party order, actions, and outcomes.
All unprofiled NPCs, monsters, named encounters, historical creators, and other dramatic individuals not directly described in the selected official story witness.
Classes, races, alignments, monsters, spells, items, dungeon levels, labyrinth, party-management, navigation, combat, and UI systems as character nodes.

The 1981 Apple II original as a separately detailed text/version; 2023 Early Access; console/PC patches; all later Wizardry titles/ports/remakes; Japanese/French/Spanish/Italian/German localization wording; adaptations; fan/community/wiki material, manuals, walkthroughs, data mines, and secondary databases.
uncertainties: The Drecom official announcement gives a short story premise, not a complete character directory or direct dialogue/item-description archive. The two records retain only names, roles, theft, and stated quest context.

Drecom states the remake builds directly on the original Apple II code while adding modern graphics and improved party-management/navigation/spellcasting/combat. It does not supply a claim-by-claim equivalence table, so original/remake narrative and mechanical identity is not assumed beyond the cited statement.
The player crafts a party, and the official material says party management and combat have changed for ease of play. No universal adventurer roster, victory, death, or relationship is asserted.

English source wording is reviewed, while the official release lists six localized languages. The 2024 IP/rightsholder statement is time-sensitive; current ownership/licensing changes after this 2024 release witness are not used to revise game continuity.
No ending, final combat result, or detailed labyrinth/amulet interpretation is recorded, avoiding unsupported spoilers.
evidence_basis: First-party Drecom IP-holder official release and IP-anniversary announcements only. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, community guide, review, walkthrough, archival manual, data mine, or secondary database is used as canonical evidence.
